title: Why thin columns buckle
examples: Why does a long straw fold when you push it?
How do engineers stop columns buckling?

marks.label: Short, stout column
marks.ask: How does a short column fail?

explain.say: Press down on a short, thick pencil stub and it holds firm. Press down on a long, thin straw and it suddenly bows out sideways and folds. That sudden sideways failure is called buckling.

marks.label: Short, stout column
marks.ask: How does a short column fail?

explain.say: A short, stout column fails only when the material itself is crushed. Stone, concrete and steel can take enormous squeezing before that happens.

marks.label: Short, stout column
marks.ask: How does a short column fail?

explain.say: But as a column gets longer and thinner, the load it can carry before buckling drops fast. Double the length and it can carry only about a quarter as much, a rule worked out by Leonhard Euler in the 1700s.

marks.label: Short, stout column
marks.ask: How does a short column fail?

explain.say: So engineers make long columns thicker, use hollow tubes or I-shapes that are stiff in every direction, and brace them partway up. Each brace effectively turns one long column into shorter ones.

marks.label: Short, stout column
marks.ask: How does a short column fail?

faq.a: A long, slender column can bend sideways under a load far smaller than what would crush its material. Once it starts to bow, the load pushes it further out, and it suddenly folds.
asks: Why does a long straw fold when you push it?

faq.q: How does a short column fail?
faq.a: A short, stout column does not buckle; it fails only when the material itself is crushed, which takes a very large load.
The buckling load falls with the square of the length: double the length and the column can carry only about a quarter of the load. Leonhard Euler worked this out in 1744.

faq.q: How do engineers stop columns buckling?
faq.a: They make columns thicker, use hollow tubes or I-sections that resist bending, and add bracing partway up so each unbraced length is shorter.
asks: How do you strengthen a thin column?

faq.q: Why are hollow tubes good columns?
faq.a: A tube puts its material far from the centre in every direction, so it resists bending, and therefore buckling, much better than a solid rod of the same weight.

facts: Leonhard Euler published the formula for the buckling load of slender columns in 1744.
The buckling load of a slender column is inversely proportional to the square of its length.

quiz.say: A slender column buckles at 100 kilonewtons. Roughly what load would buckle an identical column twice as long?
quiz.show: Twice as long: buckling load about…
quiz.why: Buckling load falls with length squared, so doubling the length divides it by four: 100 divided by 4 is 25.

wrong.1: That would be true if the load fell in simple proportion to length, but it falls with length squared.
wrong.2: Longer columns get weaker against buckling, not stronger.
